web_blocks.title: What a Valid Stage 2 Base-and-Reclaim Sequence Requires

web_blocks.html: SKHY cannot re-enter our actionable pipeline until three tape milestones confirm institutional accumulation [22]. First, shares must carve a durable floor inside or above the $81.58–$93.48 monitor band (anchored from $81.58 KRX 000660.KS parity at $580.01B / 7.11B ADSs up to TradingView Classic Pivot S2 at $93.48 = 158.66 - (186.52 - 121.34)) and trigger a 4-hour reversal turn [22]. Second, daily Bollinger Band width must contract sharply from 57.47% toward below 18% over several weeks, showing supply exhaustion [22]. Third, SKHY must reclaim its 50-day SMA ($157.01) on at least 1.5x average volume (~35.5M shares/day) after the S&P 500 exits its 10-distribution-day Downtrend [22].

book_paragraphs: If Chapter 7 showed that SKHY's 5.77x trailing earnings multiple still hides a 27.0% ADR premium and steep capital commitments, Chapter 8 reads the market's verdict straight off the November 20, 2026 tape. That verdict is brutal and unmistakable: our $116.28 structural stop has been breached.

On Friday, November 20, SKHY crashed 13.11% to close at $103.57, locking in a 21.41% weekly loss and a 48.18% decline from its $199.87 post-IPO high. During the session, shares hit a fresh 52-week low of $102.45 on nearly 39.86 million shares—1.69 times the 30-day average volume. When a stock slices through both Pivot S1 at $121.34 and your $116.28 hard stop on nearly double normal volume, debate ends and risk rules take over.

Let us disclose a technical data nuance cleanly before walking through the timeframes. Because SKHY only began trading on the NASDAQ on July 10, 2026, it has accumulated 95 daily bars as of November 20—short of the 200 daily bars required by our quantitative market-facts script to compute a 200-day moving average. As a result, the raw facts ledger records stage as null with insufficient history. Meanwhile, our snapshot evaluation engine classifies SKHY as STAGE_4 and CAP_REJECTED because every available moving average is rolling over.

Look at the multi-timeframe damage across the weekly, daily, and 4-hour charts. On the weekly chart, SKHY sits 26.70% below its 10-week exponential moving average at $141.30, with a weekly RSI of 34.30. On the daily chart, the stock trades 34.04% below its falling 50-day simple moving average at $157.01 and 23.92% below its 20-day moving average at $136.13, with a daily RSI of 30.36. On the 4-hour chart, price sits deep below the 4H 20-EMA at $124.55 and the 4H 50-SMA at $136.92, with an oversold 4H RSI of 25.14 and no reversal turn triggered.

Notice how violently volatility expanded during the breakdown. SKHY's 14-day Average True Range reached $10.33 to $10.34, which equals 9.98% of the $103.57 share price, while Finviz records 8.11% weekly and 6.01% monthly volatility (with Finviz beta still unpublished at '-') and Bollinger Band width blew out to 57.47%. In a constructive Volatility Contraction Pattern, price tightens into single-digit band widths near highs. Here, 57.47% band width and 9.98% daily ATR swings reflect forced liquidation.

The broader market confirms that SKHY is not falling in a vacuum. As of November 20, the S&P 500 sits in an official Downtrend regime with ten institutional distribution days over the past 25 sessions and just 38.8% of index stocks above their 50-day moving averages. Only three of eleven market sectors remain above their 50-day averages. Within Semiconductors specifically, just 17.0% of peers trade above their 50-day EMA and 26.0% above their 200-day EMA, as Micron (-13.89%), Western Digital (-12.02%), Seagate (-12.35%), TSMC (-9.36%), and NVIDIA (-14.01%) all sit in Stage 4.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Why Oversight Layers Fail Below the 50-Day Average
book_callouts.text: Once SKHY dropped below $157.01 and then crashed through $121.34 Pivot S1, every buyer from July through October moved underwater. Those trapped holders create overhead supply on every bounce, which is why Stage 4 markdowns require time—not hope—to repair.

book_subsections.title: Volume Liquidation, Thin U.S. Sponsorship & The Next Air Pocket
paragraphs: The ownership and volume plumbing explains why the selloff accelerated below $121.34. On November 20, 39.86 million shares changed hands, marking SKHY's eighth institutional distribution day in 25 sessions and pushing 63-day relative strength to minus 23.69% against the S&P 500. Yet Finviz shows U.S. institutional ownership at just 2.55%, with short interest at only 0.53% of float (36.42 million shares, or 1.81 days to cover).

That low U.S. institutional base means long-only pension and mutual-fund buyers have not stepped in to absorb fast-money selling. With SKHY closing at $103.57—barely above the $102.45 session low—any break below $102.45 opens a technical air pocket into our derived $81.58–$93.48 monitor band, spanning TradingView Classic Pivot S2 ($93.48, calculated as 158.66 minus 186.52 minus 121.34) down to implied Seoul KRX parity at $81.58 ($580.01 billion divided by 7.11 billion ADS equivalents).

Translate that $10.33–$10.34 daily Average True Range (9.98% of close) and 8.11% weekly / 6.01% monthly volatility (Finviz beta '-') into portfolio risk terms. With nearly 10% single-day ATR swings in an active Downtrend, SKHY lost $15.63 per share on November 20 alone—wiping out $277.65 from our small 17.764-share Schwab sleeve in six hours.

book_subsections.title: Why the Options Desk Shifted to NO_OPTIONS_EDGE
paragraphs: On November 13, our options desk kept a conditional January 2027 Bull Call Spread on standby in case the $122.20 shelf held. By November 20, the options desk downgraded SKHY to NO_OPTIONS_EDGE. Our portfolio holds zero open SKHY options contracts, and initiating new calls below all falling moving averages in a CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL stock violates our risk rules.

True, a 4-hour RSI of 25.14 and a daily RSI of 30.36 can spark violent short-covering bounces toward $121.34 Pivot S1, the $126.58 10-day SMA, or even the falling $136.13 20-day SMA—strictly technical overhead bounce ceilings rather than fundamental value. Trying to trade a dead-cat bounce in a high-volatility Stage 4 ADR (9.98% daily ATR, 8.11% weekly volatility, Finviz beta '-') during a 10-distribution-day market downtrend, however, is pure speculation. Options capital stays strictly in cash.

book_subsections.title: The Three Milestones Required Before Re-Evaluating SKHY
paragraphs: Respecting a breached stop does not mean writing off SK hynix forever. It means refusing to hold equity capital through an uncontained Stage 4 markdown while waiting for the chart to heal. Before SKHY can earn another look after January 2027 Q4 earnings, we require three objective checkpoints on the tape.

First, selling pressure must carve a durable floor around $102.45 or inside the $81.58–$93.48 monitor band (KRX parity $81.58 to Pivot S2 $93.48) and trigger a higher low on the 4-hour chart. Second, daily Bollinger Band width must compress from 57.47% down below 18% over multiple quiet weeks. Third, price must reclaim the 50-day moving average ($157.01) on at least 1.5 times average volume—roughly 35.5 million shares per day—while S&P 500 breadth recovers above 50%. Until all three boxes are checked, the trend remains broken.

Trace the overhead resistance shelf by shelf so you see why patience pays. Any sharp rebound first meets sellers at the 4-hour 20-EMA ($124.55) and 10-day SMA ($126.58), then hits heavier supply at the 20-day SMA ($136.13) and 10-week EMA ($141.30), and finally confronts trapped autumn buyers between the 50-day SMA ($157.01) and Pivot Middle ($158.66). Clearing four layered resistance ceilings requires months of institutional accumulation, not a single oversold bounce.

book_subsections.title: Why Sector Breadth Rules Out Lone-Wolf Bottom Picking
paragraphs: Experienced stage traders rarely buy an individual semiconductor stock when its entire industry group is liquidating. On November 20, TheWrap reported that only 17.0% of Semiconductors trade above their 50-day EMA and 26.0% trade above their 200-day EMA, pulling the sector rank down to 21 despite strong trailing 12-month gains. Look across the peer board from the same afternoon: Micron fell 13.89%, Western Digital dropped 12.02%, Seagate slid 12.35%, TSMC lost 9.36%, and NVIDIA fell 14.01%.

When capital rotates out of an entire hardware leadership group at once, forced fund redemptions push even high-margin winners below their moving averages. Waiting for Micron, TSMC, and NVIDIA to stabilize alongside SKHY avoids fighting a sector-wide tide. Once broader industry breadth climbs back above 50% and the S&P 500 clears its ten distribution days, the next legitimate Stage 2 leader will announce itself cleanly on heavy volume.

To summarize the technical picture in one clear mental model: Stage 4 stocks behave like falling safes while distribution volume remains elevated. Our November 13 structural stop at $116.28 existed precisely to prevent a 13% gap-down week from turning into an open-ended capital loss. Respecting that broken stop on November 20 is the exact discipline that keeps a portfolio intact through a market Downtrend.

When the tape heals—if SKHY holds $102.45 or $93.48, shrinks Bollinger Band width below 18%, and reclaims $157.01 on 35.5 million shares a day—we will gladly re-examine the stock. Until those three milestones appear, technical structure bars any fresh capital commitment.

Remember that Stage 2 discipline protects you from the worst enemy in cyclical investing: buying too early into forced liquidation simply because the stock is already down 48% from its peak. Let the base form first.
